<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en" data-theme="dark">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
<meta name="description" content="A sophisticated field guide to the types of consumer telescopes — refractors, reflectors, catadioptrics, and Dobsonians.">
<title>Telescope — A Field Guide to Consumer Telescope Types</title>
<script>
  /* Apply saved theme before first paint to avoid flashing */
  (function () {
    try {
      var t = localStorage.getItem('astrolabe-theme');
      if (t === 'light' || t === 'dark') document.documentElement.dataset.theme = t;
    } catch (e) {}
  })();
</script>
<style>
/* ============================================================
   TOKENS
============================================================ */
:root {
  --font-display: "Palatino Linotype", "Book Antiqua", Palatino, "URW Palladio L", Georgia, serif;
  --font-body: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
  --radius: 16px;
  --radius-sm: 10px;
  --header-h: 68px;
  color-scheme: dark;

  /* Dark theme (default) */
  --bg: #05080f;
  --bg-soft: #0a101d;
  --hero-a: rgba(63, 92, 168, 0.30);
  --hero-b: rgba(214, 158, 66, 0.10);
  --panel: #0d1424;
  --panel-2: #111a2e;
  --line: #1f2b47;
  --line-soft: rgba(141, 166, 214, 0.14);
  --line-strong: #35496f;
  --text: #e9eef8;
  --muted: #9fadc8;
  --accent: #e7b560;
  --accent-ink: #221503;
  --accent-2: #7cc4ff;
  --accent-3: #b79bff;
  --good: #6fd39a;
  --bad: #ff8f7a;
  --glow: rgba(231, 181, 96, 0.16);
  --shadow: 0 18px 44px rgba(2, 6, 16, 0.55);
  --diagram-fill: rgba(124, 196, 255, 0.05);
  --diagram-line: #43598a;
  --star: 255, 255, 255;
  --star-alpha: 0.9;
  --scrim: rgba(5, 8, 15, 0.72);
}
[data-theme="light"] {
  color-scheme: light;
  --bg: #f5f3ec;
  --bg-soft: #eceada;
  --hero-a: rgba(96, 140, 205, 0.20);
  --hero-b: rgba(205, 152, 60, 0.14);
  --panel: #fffdf7;
  --panel-2: #f4f1e7;
  --line: #dcd6c2;
  --line-soft: rgba(32, 44, 78, 0.10);
  --line-strong: #b3aa8c;
  --text: #222b40;
  --muted: #5b6883;
  --accent: #9d6c15;
  --accent-ink: #fffdf6;
  --accent-2: #2b76b8;
  --accent-3: #5f49c2;
  --good: #1e7f4f;
  --bad: #b8432c;
  --glow: rgba(157, 108, 21, 0.14);
  --shadow: 0 18px 40px rgba(60, 52, 24, 0.14);
  --diagram-fill: rgba(43, 118, 184, 0.06);
  --diagram-line: #9a9173;
  --star: 34, 43, 64;
  --star-alpha: 0.28;
  --scrim: rgba(245, 243, 236, 0.78);
}

/* ============================================================
   BASE
============================================================ */
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
html { scroll-behavior: smooth; scroll-padding-top: calc(var(--header-h) + 18px); }
body {
  font-family: var(--font-body);
  background: var(--bg);
  color: var(--text);
  line-height: 1.65;
  font-size: 16px;
  -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;
  transition: background-color 0.4s ease, color 0.4s ease;
}
body, .panel, .site-head, .chip, .card, .type-card, .diagram, .table-scroll, .gloss-card, .quiz-panel,
.factor, .callout, .btn, .foot, .nav a, .pill, .meta li {
  transition: background-color 0.4s ease, color 0.4s ease, border-color 0.4s ease, box-shadow 0.4s ease;
}
img, svg { display: block; max-width: 100%; }
a { color: inherit; }
button { font: inherit; color: inherit; cursor: pointer; background: none; border: none; }
:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 4px; }
::selection { background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-ink); }

.skip-link {
  position: absolute; left: -9999px; top: 0; z-index: 200;
  background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-ink);
  padding: 10px 18px; border-radius: 0 0 10px 0; font-weight: 600;
}
.skip-link:focus { left: 0; }

.wrap { max-width: 1120px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 24px; }
section { padding: 96px 0 8px; }
section:last-of-type { padding-bottom: 96px; }

.kicker {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px;
  font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.22em;
  text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent);
  margin-bottom: 18px;
}
.kicker::before { content: ""; width: 34px; height: 1px; background: var(--accent); opacity: 0.7; }
h2 {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: clamp(1.85rem, 3.6vw, 2.7rem);
  font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.15; letter-spacing: -0.01em;
  margin-bottom: 16px;
}
.section-intro { color: var(--muted); max-width: 660px; font-size: 1.05rem; margin-bottom: 48px; }
.section-head { margin-bottom: 40px; }

/* ============================================================
   HEADER
============================================================ */
.site-head {
  position: fixed; inset: 0 0 auto 0; z-index: 100; height: var(--header-h);
  background: var(--scrim);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(1.3); backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(1.3);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft);
}
.head-inner {
  max-width: 1120px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 24px;
  height: 100%; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 28px;
}
.brand { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 11px; text-decoration: none; margin-right: auto; }
.brand-mark { width: 34px; height: 34px; flex: none; }
.brand-name {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.28rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.01em;
}
.brand-tag {
  font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--muted); border-left: 1px solid var(--line-strong); padding-left: 11px; margin-left: 2px;
}
/* Themed SVG colors (var() cannot live in presentation attributes) */
.bm-core { stroke: var(--accent); }
.bm-ring { stroke: var(--accent-2); }
.bm-dot  { fill: var(--accent-2); }
#gPlanet .s1 { stop-color: var(--accent); }
#gPlanet .s2 { stop-color: var(--accent-2); }
.pl-body  { stroke: var(--accent); }
.pl-bands { stroke: var(--text); }
.pl-ring  { stroke: var(--accent-2); }
.pl-dash  { stroke: var(--line-strong); }
.pl-moon  { fill: var(--accent-2); }
.nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; }
.nav a {
  text-decoration: none; font-size: 0.86rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--muted);
  padding: 8px 13px; border-radius: 9px; position: relative;
}
.nav a:hover { color: var(--text); background: var(--line-soft); }
.nav a.active { color: var(--accent); }
.head-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; }

.theme-toggle {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px;
  padding: 8px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 999px;
  background: var(--panel); font-size: 0.82rem; font-weight: 600;
}
.theme-toggle:hover { border-color: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--glow); }
.theme-toggle .icons { position: relative; width: 17px; height: 17px; }
.theme-toggle .icons svg { position: absolute; inset: 0; transition: opacity 0.35s ease, transform 0.45s ease; }
[data-theme="dark"] .icon-sun  { opacity: 0; transform: rotate(-90deg) scale(0.6); }
[data-theme="dark"] .icon-moon { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
[data-theme="light"] .icon-sun { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
[data-theme="light"] .icon-moon { opacity: 0; transform: rotate(90deg) scale(0.6); }
.theme-label-light { display: none; }
[data-theme="light"] .theme-label-light { display: inline; }
[data-theme="light"] .theme-label-dark { display: none; }

.menu-btn {
  display: none; width: 42px; height: 42px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 10px;
  background: var(--panel); align-items: center; justify-content: center;
}
.menu-btn span, .menu-btn span::before, .menu-btn span::after {
  content: ""; display: block; width: 17px; height: 2px; background: var(--text); border-radius: 2px;
  transition: transform 0.3s ease, opacity 0.3s ease; position: relative;
}
.menu-btn span::before { position: absolute; top: -5px; }
.menu-btn span::after  { position: absolute; top: 5px; }
.nav-open .menu-btn span { background: transparent; }
.nav-open .menu-btn span::before { transform: translateY(5px) rotate(45deg); }
.nav-open .menu-btn span::after  { transform: translateY(-5px) rotate(-45deg); }

/* ============================================================
   HERO
============================================================ */
.hero {
  position: relative; overflow: hidden;
  min-height: 100svh; display: flex; align-items: center;
  padding: calc(var(--header-h) + 56px) 0 84px;
  background:
    radial-gradient(900px 520px at 78% 12%, var(--hero-a), transparent 65%),
    radial-gradient(700px 460px at 8% 92%, var(--hero-b), transparent 60%),
    var(--bg);
  transition: background 0.4s ease;
}
#stars { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
.hero::after {
  content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 140px;
  background: linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent, var(--bg)); pointer-events: none;
}
.hero-inner {
  position: relative; z-index: 2; width: 100%;
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1.15fr) minmax(0, 0.85fr);
  gap: 48px; align-items: center;
}
.hero-eyebrow {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px;
  font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.26em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--accent-2); margin-bottom: 22px;
}
.hero-eyebrow .star-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--accent-2); box-shadow: 0 0 12px 2px var(--accent-2); }
.hero h1 {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: clamp(2.7rem, 6.4vw, 4.5rem);
  font-weight: 700; line-height: 1.06; letter-spacing: -0.015em;
  margin-bottom: 24px;
}
.hero h1 em {
  font-style: italic; color: var(--accent);
  text-shadow: 0 0 42px var(--glow);
}
.hero-sub { color: var(--muted); font-size: clamp(1rem, 1.6vw, 1.15rem); max-width: 540px; margin-bottom: 36px; }
.hero-cta { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 14px; margin-bottom: 44px; }
.hero-stats { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px 34px; list-style: none; }
.hero-stats li { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
.hero-stats b { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.55rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text); line-height: 1.2; }
.hero-stats span { font-size: 0.76rem; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }

.btn {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px;
  padding: 13px 24px; border-radius: 999px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.92rem;
  text-decoration: none; border: 1px solid transparent;
}
.btn-primary { background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-ink); box-shadow: 0 10px 30px var(--glow); }
.btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 14px 36px var(--glow); }
.btn-ghost { border-color: var(--line-strong); color: var(--text); }
.btn-ghost:hover { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); transform: translateY(-2px); }
.btn:active { transform: translateY(0); }

/* Planet figure */
.hero-fig { position: relative; display: flex; justify-content: center; }
.planet-wrap { width: min(360px, 88%); position: relative; }
.planet-wrap svg { width: 100%; height: auto; overflow: visible; }
.orbit-spin { transform-origin: 160px 160px; animation: orbit 26s linear infinite; }
@keyframes orbit { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }
.planet-bob { animation: bob 7s ease-in-out infinite; }
@keyframes bob { 0%, 100% { transform: translateY(0); } 50% { transform: translateY(-9px); } }
.planet-caption {
  position: absolute; left: 50%; bottom: -34px; transform: translateX(-50%);
  font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted);
  white-space: nowrap;
}

/* ============================================================
   CHIPS / META
============================================================ */
.chip {
  display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px;
  font-size: 0.74rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--line);
  background: var(--panel-2); color: var(--muted);
}
.chip .dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; }
.chip-refractor .dot { background: var(--accent-2); box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--accent-2); }
.chip-reflector .dot { background: var(--accent); box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--accent); }
.chip-cata .dot { background: var(--accent-3); box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--accent-3); }

.legend { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 44px; }

/* ============================================================
   TYPE CARDS
============================================================ */
.types-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); gap: 26px; padding-bottom: 40px; }
.type-card {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--panel) 0%, var(--bg-soft) 100%);
  border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--radius);
  overflow: hidden; box-shadow: var(--shadow);
}
.type-card:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); }
.type-card.flash { animation: flash-ring 1.6s ease; }
@keyframes flash-ring {
  0%, 100% { box-shadow: var(--shadow); }
  25%, 65% { box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px var(--accent), 0 0 46px var(--glow); }
}
.diagram {
  position: relative; height: 158px;
  background:
    linear-gradient(var(--line-soft) 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 28px 28px,
    linear-gradient(90deg, var(--line-soft) 1px, transparent 1px) 0 0 / 28px 28px,
    var(--panel-2);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
}
.diagram svg { width: 92%; height: 88%; }
.diagram .cap {
  position: absolute; left: 14px; bottom: 10px;
  font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); opacity: 0.8;
}
.sv-tube { fill: var(--diagram-fill); stroke: var(--diagram-line); stroke-width: 2; }
.sv-part { stroke: var(--diagram-line); stroke-width: 2; fill: none; }
.sv-mirror { stroke: var(--accent); stroke-width: 3.4; stroke-linecap: round; fill: none; }
.sv-lens { stroke: var(--accent-2); stroke-width: 3.4; stroke-linecap: round; fill: none; }
.sv-ray {
  stroke: var(--accent-2); stroke-width: 1.5; fill: none; opacity: 0.85;
  stroke-dasharray: 5 7; animation: rayflow 1.15s linear infinite;
}
@keyframes rayflow { to { stroke-dashoffset: -24; } }
.sv-dot { fill: var(--accent); }
.sv-label { font: 600 9px var(--font-body); fill: var(--muted); letter-spacing: 0.1em; }

.type-body { padding: 24px 26px 26px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; flex: 1; }
.type-top { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 6px; flex-wrap: wrap; }
.type-body h3 { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; }
.type-tag { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.88rem; font-style: italic; margin-bottom: 14px; }
.type-how { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.94rem; margin-bottom: 18px; }
.type-how b { color: var(--text); font-weight: 600; }
.pcs { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 6px 20px; margin-bottom: 20px; }
.pcs ul { list-style: none; }
.pcs h4 {
  font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase;
  margin-bottom: 8px;
}
.pcs .pros h4 { color: var(--good); }
.pcs .cons h4 { color: var(--bad); }
.pcs li { font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--muted); padding: 3px 0 3px 20px; position: relative; }
.pcs .pros li::before { content: "✓"; position: absolute; left: 0; color: var(--good); font-weight: 700; }
.pcs .cons li::before { content: "–"; position: absolute; left: 2px; color: var(--bad); font-weight: 700; }
.meta {
  list-style: none; margin-top: auto;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding-top: 16px;
  display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 10px;
}
.meta li { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; }
.meta span { font-size: 0.64rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted); }
.meta b { font-size: 0.86rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text); line-height: 1.35; }
.meta b.gold { color: var(--accent); }

/* ============================================================
   COMPARISON TABLE
============================================================ */
.table-scroll {
  border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--radius); overflow: auto;
  background: var(--panel); box-shadow: var(--shadow); margin-bottom: 18px;
}
table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; min-width: 860px; font-size: 0.88rem; }
th, td { padding: 14px 16px; text-align: left; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line-soft); vertical-align: middle; }
thead th {
  font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--muted); background: var(--panel-2); position: sticky; top: 0;
}
tbody th {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap;
}
th[scope="row"], tbody th { position: sticky; left: 0; background: var(--panel); z-index: 2; border-right: 1px solid var(--line); }
tbody tr:hover td, tbody tr:hover th { background: var(--panel-2); }
tbody tr:last-child th, tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: none; }
td .sub { display: block; font-size: 0.72rem; color: var(--muted); }
.dots { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; }
.dots i { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--line-strong); opacity: 0.55; }
.dots i.on { background: var(--accent); opacity: 1; box-shadow: 0 0 7px var(--glow); }
.price { color: var(--accent); font-weight: 700; white-space: nowrap; }
.table-note { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.82rem; margin-bottom: 40px; }
.table-note b { color: var(--text); }

/* ============================================================
   BUYING GUIDE
============================================================ */
.factors { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr); gap: 22px; margin-bottom: 34px; }
.factor {
  background: var(--panel); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--radius);
  padding: 26px 26px 24px; display: flex; gap: 18px;
}
.factor:hover { border-color: var(--line-strong); transform: translateY(-3px); }
.factor .num {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 700; line-height: 1;
  color: transparent; -webkit-text-stroke: 1.2px var(--accent);
  flex: none; padding-top: 2px;
}
.factor h3 { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.15rem; margin-bottom: 8px; }
.factor p { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.92rem; }
.factor p b { color: var(--text); }

.callout {
  border: 1px solid var(--accent); border-left-width: 4px; border-radius: var(--radius-sm);
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--glow), transparent 70%);
  padding: 24px 28px; margin-bottom: 40px;
}
.callout h3 { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.1rem; color: var(--accent); margin-bottom: 8px; }
.callout p { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.95rem; }
.callout p b { color: var(--text); }

/* ============================================================
   QUIZ
============================================================ */
.quiz-panel {
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--panel) 0%, var(--bg-soft) 100%);
  border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--radius); box-shadow: var(--shadow);
  padding: clamp(24px, 4vw, 44px); margin-bottom: 40px;
}
.quiz { display: grid; gap: 34px; }
.quiz fieldset { border: none; }
.quiz legend {
  font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.2rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 16px;
}
.quiz legend .qnum { color: var(--accent); font-size: 0.95rem; margin-right: 8px; }
.pills { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 10px; }
.pill { position: relative; }
.pill input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; inset: 0; cursor: pointer; }
.pill span {
  display: inline-block; padding: 10px 18px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong);
  border-radius: 999px; font-size: 0.88rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--muted);
}
.pill input:hover + span { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--text); }
.pill input:checked + span {
  background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-ink); font-weight: 600;
  box-shadow: 0 6px 18px var(--glow);
}
.pill input:focus-visible + span { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 3px; }

.quiz-result {
  display: none; margin-top: 8px; padding-top: 28px; border-top: 1px dashed var(--line-strong);
}
.quiz-result.show { display: block; animation: rise 0.5s ease; }
@keyframes rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(14px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }
.result-label {
  font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.22em; text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--accent-2); margin-bottom: 10px;
}
.result-name { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.7rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 10px; }
.result-why { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.98rem; max-width: 620px; margin-bottom: 16px; }

<section id="types" aria-labelledby="types-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head reveal">
      <p class="kicker">01 · The Families</p>
      <h2 id="types-h">Three ways to bend starlight</h2>
      <p class="section-intro">
        Every consumer telescope is built around one of three optical strategies — lenses, mirrors,
        or a combination of both. Five designs dominate the market, each trading off light-gathering,
        portability, and upkeep in its own signature way.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="legend reveal" role="list" aria-label="Optical families">
      <span class="chip chip-refractor" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Refracting · lenses</span>
      <span class="chip chip-reflector" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Reflecting · mirrors</span>
      <span class="chip chip-cata" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric · lenses + mirrors</span>
    </div>

    <div class="types-grid stagger">

      <!-- REFRACTOR -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-refractor">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="42" y="50" width="168" height="40" rx="9"/>
            <line class="sv-lens" x1="46" y1="44" x2="46" y2="96"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="210" y="56" width="14" height="28" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 60 L46 60 L196 70 L226 66"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 70 L46 70 L196 70 L226 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 80 L46 80 L196 70 L226 74"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="18" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="188" y="116">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Refractor</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Refractor</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-refractor"><span class="dot"></span>Refracting</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The classic all-lens design</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            Light passes through a corrected <b>objective lens</b> at the front of the tube and is
            focused at the rear, where the eyepiece sits. The all-glass tube stays sealed for life —
            the original “point and go” telescope.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Zero maintenance — nothing to collimate</li>
                <li>Sharp, high-contrast Moon & planet views</li>
                <li>Compact, travel-friendly, sturdy</li>
                <li>Sealed tube keeps images steady</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Color fringing in cheaper achromats</li>
                <li>Priciest per inch of aperture</li>
                <li>Small apertures limit deep-sky detail</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Moon, planets, wide-field</b></li>
            <li><span>Entry price</span><b class="gold">from ~$200</b></li>
            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>60 – 120 mm</b></li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <!-- NEWTONIAN -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-newtonian">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="34" y="56" width="182" height="40" rx="6"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M212 52 q6 26 0 52"/>
            <line class="sv-part" x1="58" y1="56" x2="80" y2="78"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="60" y="40" width="16" height="16" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 64 L212 64 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 76 L212 76 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 88 L212 88 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="18" y="32">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="48" y="22">EYEPIECE</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="150" y="116">PRIMARY MIRROR</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Newtonian</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Newtonian Reflector</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-reflector"><span class="dot"></span>Reflecting</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The deep-sky workhorse</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            A concave <b>primary mirror</b> at the bottom of the tube reflects light back to a flat
            45° secondary, which diverts it out the side to the eyepiece. Mirrors are cheap to make
            large — which is why every serious deep-sky scope uses one.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Huge apertures for the money</li>
                <li>No chromatic aberration — ever</li>
                <li>Easy to upgrade and customize</li>
                <li>Open tube = fast image stability</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Needs occasional collimation</li>
                <li>Tubes are bulky and less portable</li>
                <li>Secondary spider blocks some light</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Deep sky, budget builders</b></li>
            <li><span>Entry price</span><b class="gold">from ~$250</b></li>
            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>130 – 250 mm</b></li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <!-- SCHMIDT-CASSEGRAIN -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-sct">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="68" y="44" width="134" height="52" rx="10"/>
            <path class="sv-lens" d="M70 42 q-7 30 0 60"/>
            <ellipse class="sv-dot" cx="71" cy="70" rx="3" ry="6.5"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 42 q-7 11 -3 22"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 98 q-7 -11 -3 -22"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="202" y="60" width="14" height="20" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 58 L200 58 L71 70 L220 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 82 L200 82 L71 70 L220 70"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="16" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="176" y="122">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Schmidt-Cassegrain</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Schmidt-Cassegrain</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-cata"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The versatile travel all-rounder</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            A <b>Schmidt corrector plate</b> feeds light to a curved primary mirror at the rear,
            which reflects it through a hole in its center to a back-mounted eyepiece — folding a
            ~2,000 mm focal length into a 40 cm tube.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Long focal length in a short tube</li>
                <li>Sealed — almost no collimation</li>
                <li>One scope for Moon, planets & deep sky</li>
                <li>GoTo-ready in almost every setup</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Slow to cool — first 20 min are soft</li>
                <li>Expensive per inch of aperture</li>
                <li>Narrower field than a reflector</li>

            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Moon & planets, travel</b></li>

            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>203 – 254 mm</b></li>

        </div>
      </article>

          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">

            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 42 q-7 11 -3 22"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 98 q-7 -11 -3 -22"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="202" y="60" width="14" height="20" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 58 L200 58 L63 70 L220 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 82 L200 82 L63 70 L220 70"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="16" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="176" y="122">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Maksutov-Cassegrain</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Maksutov-Cassegrain</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-cata"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The sharp, sealed compact</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            A thick <b>meniscus corrector lens</b> — whose back surface also acts as the tiny

          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Superb contrast for planetary work</li>
                <li>Fully sealed — no dust, no collimation</li>

            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Planetary purists</b></li>

            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>127 – 150 mm</b></li>

<!-- ================= BUYING GUIDE ================= -->
<section id="guide" aria-labelledby="guide-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head reveal">
      <p class="kicker">03 · Choosing Wisely</p>
      <h2 id="guide-h">Five decisions that matter more than the box says</h2>
      <p class="section-intro">
        Marketing copy loves big magnification numbers. Here are the criteria that actually
        determine whether a telescope earns a permanent spot in your night routine.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="factors stagger">
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">01</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Aperture first</h3>
          <p>
            The single most important spec. Aperture is the diameter of the primary lens or mirror,
            and it sets <b>how much light</b> and <b>how much detail</b> you get. Never buy
            “magnification” — it's just aperture with eyepieces swapped in.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">02</span>
        <div>
          <h3>The mount is half the telescope</h3>
          <p>
            A great optic on a wobbly mount is a toy. <b>Alt-azimuth</b> mounts are intuitive and
            GoTo-friendly; <b>equatorial</b> mounts track with one motor and enable long-exposure
            astrophotography. Budget for a sturdy mount before extra features.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">03</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Optics versus upkeep</h3>
          <p>
            Sealed refractors and catadioptrics are set-and-forget. Reflectors deliver the most
            light per dollar but need <b>collimation</b> every few months. Pick the maintenance
            level you're genuinely willing to perform.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">04</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Be honest about portability</h3>
          <p>
            If it doesn't fit in your car and on your shoulder, it won't travel. A
            <b>smaller scope used weekly</b> teaches you more than a larger one that stays
            covered in the garage. Travel size: under ~4 kg, under 70 cm.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">05</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Budget for the whole kit, not just the tube</h3>
          <p>
            A decent finderscope, a spare eyepiece, a red-light flashlight, a sturdy table, and
            dew-strap protection can run <b>10–20% of the scope's price</b>. The first eyepiece
            included with a kit is rarely the one you'll use most — a good 25 mm and a 10 mm will
            cover most nights.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="callout reveal" role="note">
      <h3>Rule of thumb</h3>
      <p>
        Start somewhere between <b>4" and 8" of aperture</b>. An 8" Dobsonian gathers roughly
        six times the light of a 4" refractor — and often costs less. Buy the biggest aperture you
        can comfortably carry and point, then upgrade eyepieces and the mount as your interest
        (and your eyes) adapt.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Aperture</dt><dd>The diameter of the main lens or mirror. The #1 spec — more aperture means more light and finer detail.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Focal length</dt><dd>The distance over which light is brought to focus. Combined with aperture, it sets your magnification range and field of view.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>f-ratio</dt><dd>Focal length ÷ aperture. “Fast” (f/4) scopes give wide fields at low power; “slow” (f/10+) give high magnification reach.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Collimation</dt><dd>Keeping all optical surfaces precisely aligned. Reflectors need it occasionally; refractors and SCTs rarely do.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Alt-azimuth</dt><dd>A two-axis mount: up/down and left/right. Intuitive to use, the default for Dobsonians and most GoTo mounts.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Equatorial</dt><dd>A two-axis mount aligned to the sky's rotation. Tracks objects with a single motor and enables long-exposure astrophotography.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>GoTo</dt><dd>A computerized mount that slews to any named object — planets, nebulae, comets — at the touch of a button.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Eyepiece</dt><dd>The small lens you look through. Magnification = focal length of the scope ÷ focal length of the eyepiece. Cheap to upgrade.</dd></div>

Content accuracy:
- Refractor: lenses only. Pros: sealed tube (no collimation), sharp crisp image, low maintenance, portable. Cons: expensive per aperture, chromatic aberration in cheap achromats, short focal length for deep sky. Best: Moon/planets, widefield, travel. Entry: ~$200 for 60-80mm.
- Newtonian: concave primary mirror + flat secondary. Pros: big aperture for the money, no chromatic aberration, easy to upgrade, open tube. Cons: needs collimation, tube blocks part of the light, bulkier. Entry: ~$250 for 6-8".
- SCT: Cassegrain with a Schmidt corrector. Pros: long focal length in a compact tube, versatile, sealed. Cons: slow to cool down, expensive per aperture, needs collimation (rarely). Entry: ~$600 for 8".
- Mak: meniscus corrector, f/12. Pros: very sharp, sealed, compact, cheaper than SCT. Cons: long focal length = low magnification, slower, narrower field. Entry: ~$400 for 127mm.
- Dobsonian: Newtonian on an alt-azimuth base. Pros: biggest aperture for the money, simple, stable base, easy. Cons: not GoTo by default (unless you add a wedge/GoTo kit), requires pointing by hand, heavy. Entry: ~$400 for 8" / $600 for 10".

Glossary terms:
- Aperture: the diameter of the main lens or mirror; the single most important spec — bigger means more light and finer detail.
- Focal length: the distance over which light is brought to a focus; combined with aperture, it sets magnification range and field of view.
- f-ratio: focal length ÷ aperture (f/4 is "fast," f/10 is "slow"); a guide to the balance of magnification vs. field.
- Collimation: keeping the optical surfaces precisely aligned; reflectors need it occasionally, refractors essentially never do.
- Alt-azimuth: a two-axis mount (up/down, left/right); intuitive to use, often GoTo-ready.
- Equatorial: a two-axis mount aligned to the sky's rotation; tracks by a single motor and enables long exposures.
- GoTo: a computerized mount that slews to named celestial objects at the touch of a button.
- Eyepiece: the small lens you look through; swapping eyepieces changes magnification.

Buying guide factors:
1. Aperture first — every rule of thumb starts here. More aperture = more light, more detail. Don't chase advertised "maximum magnification" numbers.
2. Match the mount — a great scope on a wobbly mount is a toy. Alt-az for beginners and portability; equatorial for tracking and astrophotography; GoTo for convenience.
3. Optics vs. maintenance — sealed refractors and SCTs are set-and-forget; reflectors give you the most light for the money but need occasional collimation.
4. Be honest about portability — if it won't fit in your car and on your shoulder, it will stay in the garage. A smaller scope used often beats a bigger scope used rarely.
5. Set a budget that includes accessories — a finder, spare eyepiece, red flashlight, and a sturdy table can cost 10–20% of the scope's price.

<section id="types" aria-labelledby="types-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head reveal">
      <p class="kicker">01 · The Families</p>
      <h2 id="types-h">Three ways to bend starlight</h2>
      <p class="section-intro">
        Every consumer telescope is built around one of three optical strategies — lenses, mirrors,
        or a combination of both. Five designs dominate the market, each trading off light-gathering,
        portability, and upkeep in its own signature way.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="legend reveal" role="list" aria-label="Optical families">
      <span class="chip chip-refractor" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Refracting · lenses</span>
      <span class="chip chip-reflector" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Reflecting · mirrors</span>
      <span class="chip chip-cata" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric · lenses + mirrors</span>
    </div>

    <div class="types-grid stagger">

      <!-- REFRACTOR -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-refractor">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="42" y="50" width="168" height="40" rx="9"/>
            <line class="sv-lens" x1="46" y1="44" x2="46" y2="96"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="210" y="56" width="14" height="28" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 60 L46 60 L196 70 L226 66"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 70 L46 70 L196 70 L226 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 80 L46 80 L196 70 L226 74"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="18" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="188" y="116">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Refractor</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Refractor</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-refractor"><span class="dot"></span>Refracting</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The classic all-lens design</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            Light passes through a corrected <b>objective lens</b> at the front of the tube and is
            focused at the rear, where the eyepiece sits. The all-glass tube stays sealed for life —
            the original “point and go” telescope.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Zero maintenance — nothing to collimate</li>
                <li>Sharp, high-contrast Moon & planet views</li>
                <li>Compact, travel-friendly, sturdy</li>
                <li>Sealed tube keeps images steady</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Color fringing in cheaper achromats</li>
                <li>Priciest per inch of aperture</li>
                <li>Small apertures limit deep-sky detail</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Moon, planets, wide-field</b></li>
            <li><span>Entry price</span><b class="gold">from ~$200</b></li>
            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>60 – 120 mm</b></li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <!-- NEWTONIAN -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-newtonian">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="34" y="56" width="182" height="40" rx="6"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M212 52 q6 26 0 52"/>
            <line class="sv-part" x1="58" y1="56" x2="80" y2="78"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="60" y="40" width="16" height="16" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 64 L212 64 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 76 L212 76 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 88 L212 88 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="18" y="32">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="48" y="22">EYEPIECE</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="150" y="116">PRIMARY MIRROR</text>

          <span class="cap">Light path · Newtonian</span>

            <h3>Newtonian Reflector</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-reflector"><span class="dot"></span>Reflecting</span>

          <p class="type-how">

            45° secondary, which diverts it out the side to the eyepiece. Mirrors are cheap to make
            large — which is why every serious deep-sky scope uses one.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Huge apertures for the money</li>
                <li>No chromatic aberration — ever</li>
                <li>Easy to upgrade and customize</li>
                <li>Open tube = fast image stability</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Needs occasional collimation</li>
                <li>Tubes are bulky and less portable</li>
                <li>Secondary spider blocks some light</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Deep sky, budget builders</b></li>

            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 42 q-7 11 -3 22"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 98 q-7 -11 -3 -22"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="202" y="60" width="14" height="20" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 58 L200 58 L71 70 L220 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 82 L200 82 L71 70 L220 70"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="16" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="176" y="122">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Schmidt-Cassegrain</span>

        <div class="type-body">

            <h3>Schmidt-Cassegrain</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-cata"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The versatile travel all-rounder</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            A <b>Schmidt corrector plate</b> feeds light to a curved primary mirror at the rear,
            which reflects it through a hole in its center to a back-mounted eyepiece — folding a
            ~2,000 mm focal length into a 40 cm tube.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Long focal length in a short tube</li>

            <text class="sv-label" x="16" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>

            <span class="chip chip-cata"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric</span>

<!-- ================= BUYING GUIDE ================= -->
<section id="guide" aria-labelledby="guide-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head reveal">
      <p class="kicker">03 · Choosing Wisely</p>
      <h2 id="guide-h">Five decisions that matter more than the box says</h2>
      <p class="section-intro">
        Marketing copy loves big magnification numbers. Here are the criteria that actually
        determine whether a telescope earns a permanent spot in your night routine.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="factors stagger">
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">01</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Aperture first</h3>
          <p>
            The single most important spec. Aperture is the diameter of the primary lens or mirror,
            and it sets <b>how much light</b> and <b>how much detail</b> you get. Never buy
            “magnification” — it's just aperture with eyepieces swapped in.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">02</span>
        <div>
          <h3>The mount is half the telescope</h3>
          <p>
            A great optic on a wobbly mount is a toy. <b>Alt-azimuth</b> mounts are intuitive and
            GoTo-friendly; <b>equatorial</b> mounts track with one motor and enable long-exposure
            astrophotography. Budget for a sturdy mount before extra features.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">03</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Optics versus upkeep</h3>
          <p>
            Sealed refractors and catadioptrics are set-and-forget. Reflectors deliver the most
            light per dollar but need <b>collimation</b> every few months. Pick the maintenance
            level you're genuinely willing to perform.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">04</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Be honest about portability</h3>
          <p>
            If it doesn't fit in your car and on your shoulder, it won't travel. A
            <b>smaller scope used weekly</b> teaches you more than a larger one that stays
            covered in the garage. Travel size: under ~4 kg, under 70 cm.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">05</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Budget for the whole kit, not just the tube</h3>
          <p>
            A decent finderscope, a spare eyepiece, a red-light flashlight, a sturdy table, and
            dew-strap protection can run <b>10–20% of the scope's price</b>. The first eyepiece
            included with a kit is rarely the one you'll use most — a good 25 mm and a 10 mm will
            cover most nights.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="callout reveal" role="note">
      <h3>Rule of thumb</h3>
      <p>
        Start somewhere between <b>4" and 8" of aperture</b>. An 8" Dobsonian gathers roughly
        six times the light of a 4" refractor — and often costs less. Buy the biggest aperture you
        can comfortably carry and point, then upgrade eyepieces and the mount as your interest
        (and your eyes) adapt.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

    <dl class="glossary-grid stagger">
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Aperture</dt><dd>The diameter of the main lens or mirror. The #1 spec — more aperture means more light and finer detail.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Focal length</dt><dd>The distance over which light is brought to focus. Combined with aperture, it sets your magnification range and field of view.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>f-ratio</dt><dd>Focal length ÷ aperture. “Fast” (f/4) scopes give wide fields at low power; “slow” (f/10+) give high magnification reach.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Collimation</dt><dd>Keeping all optical surfaces precisely aligned. Reflectors need it occasionally; refractors and SCTs rarely do.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Alt-azimuth</dt><dd>A two-axis mount: up/down and left/right. Intuitive to use, the default for Dobsonians and most GoTo mounts.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Equatorial</dt><dd>A two-axis mount aligned to the sky's rotation. Tracks objects with a single motor and enables long-exposure astrophotography.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>GoTo</dt><dd>A computerized mount that slews to any named object — planets, nebulae, comets — at the touch of a button.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Eyepiece</dt><dd>The small lens you look through. Magnification = focal length of the scope ÷ focal length of the eyepiece. Cheap to upgrade.</dd></div>
    </dl>

/* ============================================================
   QUIZ
============================================================ */
.quiz-panel {
  background: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--panel) 0%, var(--bg-soft) 100%);

.pills { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 10px; }

.pill span {
  display: inline-block; padding: 10px 18px; border: 1px solid var(--line-strong);

}
.pill input:hover + span { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--text); }

  background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-ink); font-weight: 600;
  box-shadow: 0 6px 18px var(--glow);
}
.pill input:focus-visible + span { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 3px; }

.quiz-result {
  display: none; margin-top: 8px; padding-top: 28px; border-top: 1px dashed var(--line-strong);
}
.quiz-result.show { display: block; animation: rise 0.5s ease; }
@keyframes rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(14px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }
.result-label {
  font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.22em; text-transform: uppercase;

}
.result-name { font-family: var(--font-display); font-size: 1.7rem; font-weight: 700; margin-bottom: 10px; }
.result-why { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.98rem; max-width: 620px; margin-bottom: 16px; }
.result-foot { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 16px; }
.result-price { font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--accent); font-weight: 700; }
.btn-sm { padding: 10px 18px; font-size: 0.84rem; }

/* ============================================================
   GLOSSARY
============================================================ */

<section id="types" aria-labelledby="types-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head reveal">
      <p class="kicker">01 · The Families</p>
      <h2 id="types-h">Three ways to bend starlight</h2>
      <p class="section-intro">
        Every consumer telescope is built around one of three optical strategies — lenses, mirrors,
        or a combination of both. Five designs dominate the market, each trading off light-gathering,
        portability, and upkeep in its own signature way.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="legend reveal" role="list" aria-label="Optical families">
      <span class="chip chip-refractor" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Refracting · lenses</span>
      <span class="chip chip-reflector" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Reflecting · mirrors</span>
      <span class="chip chip-cata" role="listitem"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric · lenses + mirrors</span>
    </div>

    <div class="types-grid stagger">

      <!-- REFRACTOR -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-refractor">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="42" y="50" width="168" height="40" rx="9"/>
            <line class="sv-lens" x1="46" y1="44" x2="46" y2="96"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="210" y="56" width="14" height="28" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 60 L46 60 L196 70 L226 66"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 70 L46 70 L196 70 L226 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 80 L46 80 L196 70 L226 74"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="18" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="188" y="116">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Refractor</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Refractor</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-refractor"><span class="dot"></span>Refracting</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The classic all-lens design</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            Light passes through a corrected <b>objective lens</b> at the front of the tube and is
            focused at the rear, where the eyepiece sits. The all-glass tube stays sealed for life —
            the original “point and go” telescope.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Zero maintenance — nothing to collimate</li>
                <li>Sharp, high-contrast Moon & planet views</li>
                <li>Compact, travel-friendly, sturdy</li>
                <li>Sealed tube keeps images steady</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Color fringing in cheaper achromats</li>
                <li>Priciest per inch of aperture</li>
                <li>Small apertures limit deep-sky detail</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Moon, planets, wide-field</b></li>
            <li><span>Entry price</span><b class="gold">from ~$200</b></li>
            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>60 – 120 mm</b></li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <!-- NEWTONIAN -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-newtonian">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="34" y="56" width="182" height="40" rx="6"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M212 52 q6 26 0 52"/>
            <line class="sv-part" x1="58" y1="56" x2="80" y2="78"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="60" y="40" width="16" height="16" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 64 L212 64 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 76 L212 76 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 88 L212 88 L72 66 L72 40"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="18" y="32">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="48" y="22">EYEPIECE</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="150" y="116">PRIMARY MIRROR</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Newtonian</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Newtonian Reflector</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-reflector"><span class="dot"></span>Reflecting</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The deep-sky workhorse</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            A concave <b>primary mirror</b> at the bottom of the tube reflects light back to a flat
            45° secondary, which diverts it out the side to the eyepiece. Mirrors are cheap to make
            large — which is why every serious deep-sky scope uses one.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Huge apertures for the money</li>
                <li>No chromatic aberration — ever</li>
                <li>Easy to upgrade and customize</li>
                <li>Open tube = fast image stability</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Needs occasional collimation</li>
                <li>Tubes are bulky and less portable</li>
                <li>Secondary spider blocks some light</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Deep sky, budget builders</b></li>
            <li><span>Entry price</span><b class="gold">from ~$250</b></li>
            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>130 – 250 mm</b></li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <!-- SCHMIDT-CASSEGRAIN -->
      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-sct">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="68" y="44" width="134" height="52" rx="10"/>
            <path class="sv-lens" d="M70 42 q-7 30 0 60"/>
            <ellipse class="sv-dot" cx="71" cy="70" rx="3" ry="6.5"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 42 q-7 11 -3 22"/>
            <path class="sv-mirror" d="M200 98 q-7 -11 -3 -22"/>
            <rect class="sv-part" x="202" y="60" width="14" height="20" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 58 L200 58 L71 70 L220 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 82 L200 82 L71 70 L220 70"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="16" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="176" y="122">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Schmidt-Cassegrain</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Schmidt-Cassegrain</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-cata"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The versatile travel all-rounder</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            A <b>Schmidt corrector plate</b> feeds light to a curved primary mirror at the rear,
            which reflects it through a hole in its center to a back-mounted eyepiece — folding a
            ~2,000 mm focal length into a 40 cm tube.
          </p>
          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Long focal length in a short tube</li>
                <li>Sealed — almost no collimation</li>
                <li>One scope for Moon, planets & deep sky</li>
                <li>GoTo-ready in almost every setup</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Slow to cool — first 20 min are soft</li>
                <li>Expensive per inch of aperture</li>
                <li>Narrower field than a reflector</li>
              </ul>
            </div>
          </div>
          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Moon & planets, travel</b></li>
            <li><span>Entry price</span><b class="gold">from ~$600 (8")</b></li>
            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>203 – 254 mm</b></li>
          </ul>
        </div>
      </article>

      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-mak">

          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">
            <rect class="sv-tube" x="70" y="44" width="132" height="52" rx="10"/>

            <rect class="sv-part" x="202" y="60" width="14" height="20" rx="4"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 58 L200 58 L63 70 L220 70"/>
            <path class="sv-ray" d="M10 82 L200 82 L63 70 L220 70"/>
            <text class="sv-label" x="16" y="30">STARLIGHT</text>
            <text class="sv-label" x="176" y="122">EYEPIECE</text>
          </svg>
          <span class="cap">Light path · Maksutov-Cassegrain</span>
        </div>
        <div class="type-body">
          <div class="type-top">
            <h3>Maksutov-Cassegrain</h3>
            <span class="chip chip-cata"><span class="dot"></span>Catadioptric</span>
          </div>
          <p class="type-tag">The sharp, sealed compact</p>
          <p class="type-how">
            A thick <b>meniscus corrector lens</b> — whose back surface also acts as the tiny

          <div class="pcs">
            <div class="pros">
              <h4>Strengths</h4>
              <ul>
                <li>Superb contrast for planetary work</li>
                <li>Fully sealed — no dust, no collimation</li>
                <li>Compact, sturdy, cheaper than SCTs</li>
                <li>Holds alignment year after year</li>

            <div class="cons">
              <h4>Watch-outs</h4>

                <li>Slower to cool than an open tube</li>

          <ul class="meta">
            <li><span>Best for</span><b>Planetary purists</b></li>
            <li><span>Entry price</span><b class="gold">from ~$400 (5")</b></li>
            <li><span>Typical aperture</span><b>127 – 150 mm</b></li>

        </div>

      <article class="type-card reveal" id="card-dob" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
        <div class="diagram" aria-hidden="true">
          <svg viewBox="0 0 260 140">

<!-- ================= BUYING GUIDE ================= -->
<section id="guide" aria-labelledby="guide-h">
  <div class="wrap">
    <div class="section-head reveal">
      <p class="kicker">03 · Choosing Wisely</p>
      <h2 id="guide-h">Five decisions that matter more than the box says</h2>
      <p class="section-intro">
        Marketing copy loves big magnification numbers. Here are the criteria that actually
        determine whether a telescope earns a permanent spot in your night routine.
      </p>
    </div>

    <div class="factors stagger">
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">01</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Aperture first</h3>
          <p>
            The single most important spec. Aperture is the diameter of the primary lens or mirror,
            and it sets <b>how much light</b> and <b>how much detail</b> you get. Never buy
            “magnification” — it's just aperture with eyepieces swapped in.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">02</span>
        <div>
          <h3>The mount is half the telescope</h3>
          <p>
            A great optic on a wobbly mount is a toy. <b>Alt-azimuth</b> mounts are intuitive and
            GoTo-friendly; <b>equatorial</b> mounts track with one motor and enable long-exposure
            astrophotography. Budget for a sturdy mount before extra features.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">03</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Optics versus upkeep</h3>
          <p>
            Sealed refractors and catadioptrics are set-and-forget. Reflectors deliver the most
            light per dollar but need <b>collimation</b> every few months. Pick the maintenance
            level you're genuinely willing to perform.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">04</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Be honest about portability</h3>
          <p>
            If it doesn't fit in your car and on your shoulder, it won't travel. A
            <b>smaller scope used weekly</b> teaches you more than a larger one that stays
            covered in the garage. Travel size: under ~4 kg, under 70 cm.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="factor reveal" style="grid-column: 1 / -1;">
        <span class="num" aria-hidden="true">05</span>
        <div>
          <h3>Budget for the whole kit, not just the tube</h3>
          <p>
            A decent finderscope, a spare eyepiece, a red-light flashlight, a sturdy table, and
            dew-strap protection can run <b>10–20% of the scope's price</b>. The first eyepiece
            included with a kit is rarely the one you'll use most — a good 25 mm and a 10 mm will
            cover most nights.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="callout reveal" role="note">
      <h3>Rule of thumb</h3>
      <p>
        Start somewhere between <b>4" and 8" of aperture</b>. An 8" Dobsonian gathers roughly
        six times the light of a 4" refractor — and often costs less. Buy the biggest aperture you
        can comfortably carry and point, then upgrade eyepieces and the mount as your interest
        (and your eyes) adapt.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section id="glossary" aria-labelledby="gloss-h">
  <div class="wrap">

      <h2 id="gloss-h">A pocket glossary</h2>
      <p class="section-intro">The eight terms that cover 90% of every spec sheet and forum thread.</p>
    </div>

    <dl class="glossary-grid stagger">
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Aperture</dt><dd>The diameter of the main lens or mirror. The #1 spec — more aperture means more light and finer detail.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Focal length</dt><dd>The distance over which light is brought to focus. Combined with aperture, it sets your magnification range and field of view.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>f-ratio</dt><dd>Focal length ÷ aperture. “Fast” (f/4) scopes give wide fields at low power; “slow” (f/10+) give high magnification reach.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Collimation</dt><dd>Keeping all optical surfaces precisely aligned. Reflectors need it occasionally; refractors and SCTs rarely do.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Alt-azimuth</dt><dd>A two-axis mount: up/down and left/right. Intuitive to use, the default for Dobsonians and most GoTo mounts.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Equatorial</dt><dd>A two-axis mount aligned to the sky's rotation. Tracks objects with a single motor and enables long-exposure astrophotography.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>GoTo</dt><dd>A computerized mount that slews to any named object — planets, nebulae, comets — at the touch of a button.</dd></div>
      <div class="gloss-card reveal"><dt>Eyepiece</dt><dd>The small lens you look through. Magnification = focal length of the scope ÷ focal length of the eyepiece. Cheap to upgrade.</dd></div>
    </dl>

      }, { threshold: 0.05 }).observe(canvas);
    }
    document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", function () {
      if (document.hidden) stop();
      else if (visible) start();
    });
    window.addEventListener("resize", resize, { passive: true });
    resize();
    if (!reducedMotion && visible) start();

    return { applyTheme: function () { if (reducedMotion) drawStatic(); } };
  })();

  /* ---------- Reveal on scroll ---------- */
  $$(".stagger").forEach(function (group) {
    $$(".reveal", group).forEach(function (el, i) {
      el.style.setProperty("--d", (i % 4) * 90 + "ms");
    });
  });
  if ("IntersectionObserver" in window && !reducedMotion) {
    var io = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
      entries.forEach(function (e) {
        if (e.isIntersecting) { e.target.classList.add("in"); io.unobserve(e.target); }
      });
    }, { threshold: 0.12, rootMargin: "0px 0px -6% 0px" });
    $$(".reveal").forEach(function (el) { io.observe(el); });
  } else {
    $$(".reveal").forEach(function (el) { el.classList.add("in"); });
  }

  /* ---------- Nav scroll-spy ---------- */
  var spyLinks = $$(".nav a[data-spy]");
  if ("IntersectionObserver" in window && spyLinks.length) {
    var spy = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
      entries.forEach(function (e) {
        if (e.isIntersecting) {
          spyLinks.forEach(function (a) {
            a.classList.toggle("active", a.dataset.spy === e.target.id);
          });
        }
      });
    }, { rootMargin: "-38% 0px -55% 0px" });
    $$("main section[id]").forEach(function (sec) { spy.observe(sec); });
  }

  /* ---------- Back to top ---------- */
  var toTop = $("#toTop");
  var onScroll = function () {
    toTop.classList.toggle("show", window.scrollY > 640);
  };
  window.addEventListener("scroll", onScroll, { passive: true });
  onScroll();
  toTop.addEventListener("click", function () {
    window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: reducedMotion ? "auto" : "smooth" });
  });

  /* ---------- Quiz ---------- */
  var RECS = {
    refractor: {
      name: "A classic refractor",
      why: "Sealed, maintenance-free optics and easy portability make it the friendliest first scope — and the one you'll actually carry on trips.",
      price: "from ~$200 · 60–80 mm",
      card: "card-refractor"
    },
    newtonian: {
      name: "A Newtonian reflector",
      why: "Big, inexpensive apertures and zero color aberration — the deep-sky workhorse that hands you the most light per dollar.",
      price: "from ~$250 · 6–8 inch",
      card: "card-newtonian"
    },
    sct: {
      name: "A Schmidt-Cassegrain",
      why: "A long focal length folded into a short, sealed tube — one scope for the Moon, the planets, and a taste of deep sky, with GoTo options galore.",
      price: "from ~$600 · 8 inch",
      card: "card-sct"
    },
    mak: {
      name: "A Maksutov-Cassegrain",
      why: "Sealed, razor-sharp, and compact with superb planetary contrast — the pick when polish, portability, and set-and-forget matter most.",
      price: "from ~$400 · 5 inch",
      card: "card-mak"
    },
    dob: {
      name: "A Dobsonian",
      why: "The biggest aperture you can carry on your shoulder. Dead simple, rock-solid, and unbeatable for galaxies, nebulae, and star clusters.",
      price: "from ~$400 · 8–10 inch",
      card: "card-dob"
    }
  };
  var SCORES = {
    budget: {
      low:  { refractor: 2, newtonian: 1 },
      mid:  { newtonian: 2, refractor: 1, mak: 1, dob: 1 },
      high: { mak: 2, sct: 2, newtonian: 1 },
      top:  { sct: 2, newtonian: 2, dob: 2, mak: 1 }
    },
    experience: {
      first:  { refractor: 2, sct: 1, mak: 1 },
      some:   { sct: 1, mak: 1, newtonian: 1, dob: 1 },
      expert: { dob: 2, newtonian: 2, refractor: 1 }
    },
    priority: {
      deepsky:  { dob: 3, newtonian: 2 },
      planets:  { sct: 2, mak: 2, refractor: 1 },
      portable: { refractor: 2, mak: 1, sct: 1 },
      allround: { sct: 2, mak: 1, newtonian: 1 }
    }
  };
  var TIEBREAK = ["sct", "dob", "mak", "refractor", "newtonian"];

  var form = $("#quizForm");
  var result = $("#quizResult");
  var resultName = $("#resultName");
  var resultWhy = $("#resultWhy");
  var resultPrice = $("#resultPrice");
  var resultLink = $("#resultLink");
  var answered = 0;

  function compute() {
    var vals = {};
    $$("#quizForm input:checked").forEach(function (input) { vals[input.name] = input.value; });
    answered = Object.keys(vals).length;
    if (answered < 3) { result.classList.remove("show"); return; }

    var score = {};
    Object.keys(vals).forEach(function (q) {
      var adds = SCORES[q] && SCORES[q][vals[q]];
      if (adds) Object.keys(adds).forEach(function (k) { score[k] = (score[k] || 0) + adds[k]; });
    });
    var best = null, bestScore = -1;
    TIEBREAK.forEach(function (k) {
      if ((score[k] || 0) > bestScore) { bestScore = score[k] || 0; best = k; }
    });
    if (!best) best = "sct";

    var rec = RECS[best];
    resultName.textContent = rec.name;
    resultWhy.textContent = rec.why;
    resultPrice.textContent = rec.price;
    resultLink.href = "#" + rec.card;
    result.classList.add("show");
    result.dataset.card = rec.card;
  }

  form.addEventListener("change", function (e) {
    if (e.target && e.target.name) { answered = answered; compute(); }
  });

  resultLink.addEventListener("click", function () {
    var card = document.getElementById(result.dataset.card || "");
    if (card) {
      card.classList.remove("flash");
      // force reflow so the animation can restart
      void card.offsetWidth;
      card.classList.add("flash");
    }
  });
})();
</script>
